title: A Scholarship for the Prom
premise: Yara Halloran, a scholarship student at Marrow Creek Academy, has spent the semester invisible—until her only friend, Priya, vanishes on prom night, leaving behind a ring of keys stamped with dates going back decades. Following the keys, Yara uncovers the school's 'Founders' Scholarship': every generation, one student is chosen to disappear so the town's founding families can keep their fortune and their secret buried beneath the gymnasium. With the help of Theo, a founder's grandson who chose loyalty over truth once before, Yara races to expose the ritual before this year's prom seals Priya's fate—and her own. In the end, Yara trades her silence for testimony, the scholarship is abolished, and Priya is pulled alive from the old cistern, but Yara learns justice came at the cost of the town ever trusting her again.
about_author: Sebastian Okafor is a former night-shift security guard at three different boarding schools, where he collected more ghost stories than paychecks. He writes young adult fiction about kids who see through institutions that adults pretend not to.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes Marrow Creek Academy's glittering surface and Yara's careful invisibility as a scholarship kid: perfect notes, no questions, lunch in the library. Only Priya Osei has cracked her shell. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, and the fragile warmth of one real friendship.

chapters.title: The Keys Under the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, two days before prom. Priya, restless and curious, finds an old brass keyring in the gym wall while retrieving a lost earring—each key tagged with a year, 1954 to now. She jokes about a treasure hunt; Yara begs her to leave it alone. Beat: dread disguised as banter.

chapters.title: Prom Night, Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Prom unfolds in the gymnasium over the sealed sub-basement. Priya texts a photo of the keyring and one word—'found it'—then goes silent. By midnight her chair is empty, her shoes still by the punch table. Beat: the exact moment ordinary life breaks.

chapters.title: Missing, But Not Missing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Police call Priya a runaway; the school offers counseling pamphlets and moves on within a week. Yara notices adults flinching at the word 'gymnasium.' She keeps Priya's locker combination memorized. Beat: gaslit grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Keys Open
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Testing the keys one by one: a maintenance closet, a display case of founder portraits, and finally a rusted door beneath the bleachers leading down toward the cistern. The last key doesn't fit anything—yet. Beat: first physical proof the school hides something.

chapters.title: The Founder's Grandson
chapters.summary: Theo Whitlock's POV. Theo recognizes Yara snooping and panics—his family built the school, and he knows what the keys mean because his older sister 'transferred away' in 2009. He warns Yara off, then can't sleep. Beat: guilt meeting curiosity.

chapters.title: Scholarship Terms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the archive, Yara finds the Founders' Scholarship charter: each cycle, one 'merit student' receives full funding—and a one-way obligation. Every recipient's file ends with a forwarding address that doesn't exist. Beat: the horror of paperwork hiding a ritual.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo shows Yara his sister's last letter, postmarked from nowhere, describing 'the room under the water.' He confesses he found it years ago and said nothing to protect his family name. Beat: shame, and the first alliance.

chapters.title: The Cistern Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Nighttime descent through the sub-basement: flooded tunnels, carved initials, decades of scratched tallies on the walls. They find Priya's hair tie snagged on a grate. The final door needs the unmatched key. Beat: claustrophobic hope.

chapters.title: Loyalty Has a Price List
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's grandmother confronts him gently, offering him a place on the board if he lets this go—the same offer she made his father. He realizes loyalty in Marrow Creek means complicity. Beat: temptation framed as love.

chapters.title: Someone Was Kept Alive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Evidence in the tunnels—fresh water bottles, a working light, chalk marks counting days—proves recipients aren't killed but held until they sign silence agreements. Someone may still be down there. Beat: horror pivoting to urgency.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Discrepancy
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cross-referencing yearbooks, Yara maps nine vanished students across seventy years, all scholarship kids, all 'transferred' in spring. The pattern is generational, deliberate, funded. Beat: cold clarity—the scale of it.

chapters.title: A Witness Who Signed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They track down Dana Reyes, class of 1998, who took the money and the NDA. She describes the ritual: chosen at prom, 'honored' below, released changed. She begs them to stop—not for the school's sake, but theirs. Beat: fear wearing wisdom's face.

chapters.title: Ratified
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The school announces Yara herself has been awarded next year's Founders' Scholarship. The trap isn't hidden anymore—it's an honor. Her mother, drowning in medical bills, is thrilled. Beat: the trap closing with applause.

chapters.title: Mother Knows Best, Or Does She
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara almost accepts—refusing would expose everything prematurely and maybe doom Priya. She lies to her mother for the first time, forging refusal papers she'll never send. Beat: the cost of the mission turning personal.

chapters.title: The Unmatched Key
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo realizes the final key fits the founder's crypt in the cemetery chapel, where the original covenant is kept—a contract signed by every generation, including his own hand at sixteen. Beat: inheritance revealed as indictment.

chapters.title: Covenant
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reading the covenant aloud in the crypt: the town's entire economy was built on the arrangement; ending it bankrupts everyone, including Yara's scholarship and her mother's hospital charity. Truth has a body count too. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Countdown to Courtship
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. This year's 'ceremony' is moved up—prom rescheduled as a 'Founders' Gala' where Priya will be formally processed before being quietly relocated. Three days. Yara and Theo plan to get inside the sub-basement during the gala itself. Beat: ticking clock.

chapters.title: Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Amid chandeliers, Yara pickpockets the headmaster's master key while Theo triggers a fire alarm in the east wing as cover. They slip below as the school sings its founding hymn overhead. Beat: heist tension, hearts hammering.

chapters.title: Under the Water
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The cistern chamber: Priya alive, weak, guarded by two aging trustees who genuinely believe they're preserving the town. Confrontation turns violent when the alarm above forces the trustees to choose between the secret and the fire. Beat: climax—loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara chooses truth over safety: instead of fleeing, she walks Priya up through the gala itself, in front of four hundred witnesses, and reads the covenant aloud from the stage. Theo stands beside her, naming his family. The trustees don't run—they simply stop pretending. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: After the Music Stops
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue tone. Investigations begin; the scholarship becomes a reparations fund; some classmates forgive, most don't. Priya recovers; Yara loses the scholarship and gains something harder—an honest name. Final image: two girls locking the cistern door and mailing the key to Dana Reyes. Beat: bittersweet resolution.
